questions.q: An org's Data Storage usage is well under its limit, but uploads are failing with a storage error. What's the most likely explanation?
options: Salesforce has no separate limit for files
File Storage is a separate allocation from Data Storage and may be the one that's full
The org must be on an edition that doesn't support file uploads
Data Storage and File Storage are tracked as one combined allocation
questions.explain: Data Storage (records) and File Storage (attachments, files, Content Documents) are tracked and enforced as separate allocations, so one can be exhausted while the other has headroom.

questions.q: A team runs a bulk data load of one million records, then immediately checks Setup > Storage Usage and sees no change. What should they conclude?
options: The load silently failed
Those records don't count toward storage
Storage usage is calculated asynchronously, so the figure lags behind a recent load
Storage Usage only reflects File Storage, never Data Storage
questions.explain: Data and file storage are calculated asynchronously, so a large recent load may not be reflected on the Storage Usage page immediately.

questions.q: A custom object has 5 fields; another custom object has 200 fields including a large text area. Both have 10,000 records. How do their data storage costs typically compare?
options: The 200-field object costs roughly 40x more storage
Storage cost is calculated only from required fields, so the comparison depends on how many fields are required
Large text area fields are excluded entirely from any object's storage calculation
They are roughly comparable per record, since most records count toward storage at a small, fixed amount regardless of field count
questions.explain: For the vast majority of standard and custom object records, storage is counted at a small fixed amount per record rather than by actual field count or field size, so row count — not field width — is the real cost driver.

questions.q: Which of the following is the architecturally correct first concern when projecting future storage needs for a growing org?
options: Which objects or automations are creating the largest volume of new records over time
How many custom fields were added to objects this quarter
Whether page layouts have too many sections
How many validation rules are active on the busiest object
questions.explain: Because record count drives storage cost far more than field width does, the right forecasting focus is identifying which integrations or processes are generating records at volume, and at what rate.

questions.q: A record is deleted from a custom object but is still sitting in the Recycle Bin. What is true of its storage impact?
options: It immediately stops counting against the org's data storage allocation
It counts double while in the Recycle Bin
Recycle Bin contents are tracked under File Storage instead of Data Storage
It continues to count against storage until it's purged or ages out of the Recycle Bin
questions.explain: A deleted record remains in the Recycle Bin and still counts against the org's storage allocation until it is purged or expires out of the bin — deletion alone doesn't free the storage instantly.
